text:
ryan: quick alert 1: deploy-bot shows npm got tagged `next` with 1.0.0-rc.2 but PyPI has 1.0.0 final. this happened during the change window. we have a docs snippet referencing 1.0.0 too. thoughts on how to reconcile?

sofia: whoa. did we mean to cut final now? i thought final was gated until the release meeting tomorrow. can we see the pipeline run? :mag_right:

ci-bot: deploy-bot pipeline run 1749998876: job publish-npm completed (exit 0) -> tag applied `next: 1.0.0-rc.2`. job publish-pypi completed (exit 0) -> version pushed 1.0.0.

devin: looks like an inconsistent bump in the release branch. package.json stayed at 1.0.0-rc.2 but pyproject bumped to 1.0.0. human error during last PR.

priya: okay remediation options: (A) yank PyPI 1.0.0 and push 1.0.1 rc/final later; (B) republish npm as 1.0.0 final (but npm already has rc.2 so we'd need 1.0.0 final as new dist-tag); (C) leave as-is and call out mismatch in release notes (not ideal).

ryan: npm can accept 1.0.0 final if we bump and publish. but npm now has rc.2 and dist-tag `next`. if we push final with the same content it should be fine. PyPI already has final which is the blocker for republishing py.

sofia: we should avoid yanking final on PyPI. yanking breaks reproducibility and some infra pins. prefer to publish npm final to match PyPI. that keeps both registries final at 1.0.0.

deploy-bot: permission check: npm publish requires token with write:packages. current pipeline token scope: write:packages, read:packages 1. ok.

devin: i'll open a tiny PR to bump package.json to 1.0.0 on release/1.0.0 branch and trigger the publish job manually. keep changelog identical.

priya: before we push final to npm, can we smoke in prod-preview? publish with `--tag staging` then `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.0.0 latest` after smoke.

ryan: agreed. my suggested commands: `npm publish --tag staging` then run smoke harness; if green: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.0.0 latest && npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts next`.

ci-bot: note: release automation will attempt to remove `next` tag when promoting to latest but manual removal is fine.

sofia: doc change: we must update docs site that currently hardcodes `@redwood/sdk@1.0.0-rc.2` example. i'll push a patch to docs to use `@redwood/sdk@latest` instead.

devin: bump PR merged, CI green, publishing staging now. output: `published @redwood/sdk-ts@1.0.0 to registry (tag: staging)`

ryan: running smoke tests against prod-preview: basic generate/chat/embeddings scenarios. first two tests pass, embeddings latency slightly higher but within SLO.

priya: okay promote to latest when ready. note: release-manager wanted the beta badge removed from console for final - i'll coordinate a small docs redeploy after promotion.

ryan: promoted: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-ts@1.0.0 latest` && `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-ts next`. `npm dist-tag ls @redwood/sdk-ts` -> latest: 1.0.0

devin: double-checking PyPI: pristine 1.0.0 exists and files match npm package contents (tests confirm code parity).

sofia: thanks team. release-manager: do we still send scheduled release notes / deprecation?

release-manager: yes — send as planned. update in notes: mention there was a brief rc vs final mismatch caught and fixed during the change window, but no behavioral changes. adding an internal note for infra/team pins.

priya: final checklist: docs updated to `latest`, console badge removed, release notes updated, support/CS notified. i'm tagging support now.

ci-bot: pipeline cleanup: closed stale `rc` artifacts from the CDN (invalidated).

ryan: closing loop: npm & PyPI aligned on 1.0.0, docs patched, smoke tests green. will monitor telemetry for 1h. thanks all. :rocket:
